title: An explicit fourth-root correction to unary determinization
short: Sharper bounds for removing machine branching
plain: The claim sharply narrows the worst-case size of a machine reading one repeated symbol after its branching is removed.
who: Alpoge–Claude’s stipulated RH theorem (2026); Marc Deléglise and Jean-Louis Nicolas, The Landau function and the Riemann Hypothesis (2019); Viliam Geffert, Magic numbers in the state hierarchy of finite automata (2007).
statement: Let D(n) be the maximum, over languages accepted by one-way nondeterministic finite automata with at most n states over a one-letter alphabet, of the number of states in their minimal complete deterministic automata. Use a single initial state and no ε-transitions. Put Q_n = [√(li⁻¹(n−1)) − log D(n)] / [(n−1)log(n−1)]^(1/4), where log is natural and li(x)=PV∫₀ˣdt/log t, inverted on x>1. Set A=(2−√2)/3 and c=Σρ 1/|ρ(ρ+1)|, summing over all nontrivial zeta zeros with multiplicity. Then A−c ≤ liminf Q_n ≤ limsup Q_n ≤ A+c. The endpoints are approximately 0.149144501454 and 0.241379790297. Consequently D(n)=exp(√(li⁻¹(n−1))−Θ((n log n)^(1/4))).
derivation:
1. The stipulated theorem riemannHypothesis supplies ordinary RH. No additional L-function hypothesis or simplicity assumption is needed. [Announcement](https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf).
2. Let g(m) be Landau’s function, the maximum order of a permutation of m objects. Deléglise–Nicolas, Theorem 1.1(v), states under RH: “(2−√2)/3−c ≤ lim inf a_n ≤ lim sup a_n ≤ (2−√2)/3+c”, where equation (1.9) defines a_m=[√(li⁻¹(m))−log g(m)]/(m log m)^(1/4), and equation (1.11) defines c. Their equation (1.7) also gives log g(m)∼√(m log m). [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.07664).
3. Geffert, Theorem 3.7, bounds the equivalent DFA size for every unary NFA with at most n>1 states by “d ≤ F(n−1)+(n²−2)”. Theorem 5.2 states “Gmax(n)=F(n−1)+k_n”, with k_n∈{0,…,n²−2}; Gmax concerns languages whose minimal NFA has exactly n states. These provide witnesses for our at-most-n maximum. His equation (1) defines F as the largest least common multiple of a partition of n, so F=g. His Section 2 specifies precisely the automaton model above. Therefore g(n−1)≤D(n)≤g(n−1)+n²−2. [Published paper](https://im.saske.sk/hospodar/literature/2007_geffert_IC_magic_numbers.pdf).
4. The preceding growth estimate implies (n²−2)/g(n−1)→0. Hence 0≤log D(n)−log g(n−1)≤log(1+(n²−2)/g(n−1))≤(n²−2)/g(n−1)=o(1). Dividing by [(n−1)log(n−1)]^(1/4) gives Q_n=a_(n−1)+o(1). Thus both limiting bounds transfer exactly. Since A−c>0, the stated negative fourth-root correction follows.
why_new: I read the entire announcement: it contains no corollary list and no automata consequence. Searches combined ‘Riemann hypothesis’ with ‘unary automata’, ‘determinization’, ‘determinisation’, ‘state complexity’, ‘logarithmic integral’, ‘Geffert’, and the numerical constants; none produced this correction. The papers establish its separate ingredients, but neither states this automata conclusion. Existing bounds expressed through Landau’s function remain valid; the proposed novelty is their explicit signed analytic correction. Deléglise–Nicolas’s Corollary 1.3 makes the corresponding normalized Landau estimate RH-equivalent, reinforcing that this is not merely an already-unconditional analytic estimate.
doubt: Novelty is the weakest point: the transfer is short once these papers are juxtaposed and may be unpublished folklore. The searches support ‘not found explicitly stated’, not a definitive priority claim.
